record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
record.original_question: If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has a compatible inner product, meaning an inner product invariant under conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators, is the locally convex topological completion obtained by adding elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces isomorphic to its Hilbert space completion as a locally convex topological vector space with grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form?

evidence.quote: If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has an inner product invariant under the conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators (we call it a compatible inner product), then this graded state space also has a Hilbert space completion.

Conjecture 2.3. If the graded state space of a genus-zero full conformal field theory has a compatible inner product, then the locally convex topological completion obtained by adding elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces and the Hilbert space completion are isomorphic as locally convex topological vector spaces with grading structures and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian forms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V = \bigoplus_{n} V_{(n)}$ be the graded state space of a genus-zero full two-dimensional conformal field theory, viewed as a graded vector space equipped with a family of "conformal field" operators built from intertwining operators of the underlying vertex operator algebra structure. An inner product $(\cdot,\cdot)$ on $V$ is called a compatible inner product if it is a nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form which is invariant under all conformal fields constructed from intertwining operators. Given such a compatible inner product, one obtains:

(a) a Hilbert space completion $\mathcal{H}$ of $V$ with respect to the norm induced by $(\cdot,\cdot)$; and

(b) a locally convex topological completion $\widetilde{V}$ of $V$ obtained by adjoining the elements corresponding to correlation functions on higher-genus Riemann surfaces (i.e., the completion with respect to the family of seminorms produced by evaluating correlation functions on Riemann surfaces of all genera).

Both $\mathcal{H}$ and $\widetilde{V}$ carry a grading and a nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form extending those on $V$.

Question: Are $\widetilde{V}$ and $\mathcal{H}$ isomorphic as locally convex topological vector spaces equipped with the grading structure and nondegenerate symmetric Hermitian form?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as an open problem in Huang's list of open problems in mathematical 2D CFT. Subsequent literature (e.g., Moriwaki's work on full vertex algebras and Huang's papers on convergence in CFT) discusses related completion and convergence questions but does not resolve this specific identification of the higher-genus locally convex completion with the Hilbert space completion. No source found that claims a proof or counterexample.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 2.3 states that the locally convex topological completion obtained by adding elements corresponding to higher-genus Riemann surfaces and the Hilbert space completion are isomorphic.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Convergence in Conformal Field Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses convergence and completion issues in CFT, related to but not resolving the Hilbert completion conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Related convergence questions remain active research with no proof of the conjecture noted.

status_evidence.title: Two-dimensional conformal field theory, full vertex algebra and current-current deformation
status_evidence.snippet: Develops full vertex algebra framework but does not establish isomorphism of higher-genus and Hilbert space completions.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the conjecture appears in this line of work.
